newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Menem's province slams Argentine "agents of hate".
newsitem.headline: Menem's province slams Argentine "agents of hate".

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem's native province, La Rioja, on Wednesday leapt to his defence against allegations of improper financing of an airstrip, a house and a cabin he uses in his tiny hometown.

Since the private television channel America 2 took off the air last week an investigation into Menem's hometown of Anillaco in the northwest, the Argentine media, alleging censorship, has put the spotlight on grandiose building projects in the town.

"The people of La Rioja, and especially Anillaco, feel persecuted by this conspiratorial and irresponsible action by agents of hate and resentment," the provincial government, run by Menem's Peronist Party, said in a statement.

The media is asking who paid for a new full-length airstrip for a town of just 850 people -- conveniently sited for Menem, a keen pilot, to land his presidential jet on weekend visits to his country home and nearby mountain refuge.
La Rioja officials dismissed all the allegations as "ridiculous barbarities" and scheduled a public demonstration of solidarity with the Peronist leader for Thursday night.
"It will be a demonstration of support to defend him against all these attacks," said one local official, who asked not to be named. "People here are upset."

Menem has called the journalists behind the report "miserable liars...paid by the opposition." His aides say questions raised about who paid for his ranch-style home are unfounded, since he started it before taking office in 1989.
"He has been building it brick by brick for 12 years," the government of La Rioja said in a statement.
America 2 eventually broadcast the television report to fend off allegations of censorship before the channel scrapped the whole series.
The report also alleged that a mountain refuge used by Menem, which has an artificial lake and heliport, is on state land.
Menem's aides deny the log cabin belongs to him, saying it is loaned by a friend. Local officials say paperwork shows it is a nature reserve belonging to a man called Aldo Semino.
But La Nacion newspaper, giving a description of the cabin down to photos of Menem's family inside, reported that the papers are not in order and the cabin really belongs to the state.
As for the runway, at 2,400 yards almost as long as Buenos Aires' second airport, officials say it was built with Air Force help because of its "vital importance".

"It will be of great commercial importance as it's right at the centre of a zone that produces $30 million of olives a year, as well as jojoba, grapes and leather, with no rapid exit to the rest of the country," one La Rioja official said.

But Clarin newspaper reported that while some material was donated by private business, the Air Force participation was paid from "reserved funds" -- unaccountable funds held by some ministries, the presidency and the intelligence services.
